metadata.title: Nothing to Push Against
metadata.register: formal, undergrad/grad audience, no casual narration
metadata.branding: none — unbranded, book content only, no channel/logo/handle

beats.narration_text: In empty space there is nothing to push against. So how does a rocket accelerate?
beats.new_visual_element: Portrait-only opening question card (title-styled, crimson underline).

beats.narration_text: A car pushes against the road, and a swimmer pushes against the water. In the emptiness of space there is no road, no water, and no air. So how does a rocket accelerate when there is nothing to push against?
beats.new_visual_element: A road strip with a small car whose wheel pushes back on it (short arrow), then the road dissolves into empty space with a few sparse stars; a rocket floats alone in the void.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: rocket alone in empty space, sparse stars

beats.narration_text: The rocket carries its own fuel. Treat the rocket and its fuel together as one system, initially at rest. With no external force acting, the total momentum of that system is zero, and it must stay zero.
beats.new_visual_element: A dashed outline encloses the rocket and its fuel tank, labeled system; a label p_total = 0 sits beneath it.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: rocket with fuel in a dashed system boundary, total momentum zero

beats.narration_text: The engine ejects a small mass of hot gas backward at high speed, relative to the rocket. That gas now carries momentum toward the left, so the rocket must gain an equal momentum toward the right. Mass times change in velocity equals ejected mass times exhaust speed.
beats.new_visual_element: A vermilion puff of exhaust Δm shoots left with a long arrow u; at the same instant the rocket nudges right with a short arrow Δv. Equation above: m Δv = Δm u.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: exhaust puff moving left, rocket moving right, momentum equation

beats.narration_text: Keep burning, and the rocket ejects a steady stream of gas. Each bit of exhaust carries the same momentum, but the rocket that remains has less and less mass. So the same push produces a larger change in velocity each time, and the acceleration grows as the fuel runs out.
beats.new_visual_element: A continuous stream of vermilion exhaust dots flows left; the rocket's fuel gauge drains (m → 0.8m → 0.6m → 0.4m) while its velocity arrow lengthens and it moves right faster and faster.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: rocket accelerating right with a long exhaust trail, mass label decreasing, velocity arrow growing

beats.narration_text: There was never anything to push against. The rocket pushes on its own exhaust, the exhaust pushes back on the rocket, and the total momentum of the system stays zero throughout.
beats.new_visual_element: The rocket exits right, leaving the exhaust trail; the equation m Δv = Δm u stays at the top and a final line reads: no road, no air, just momentum conserved.
beats.accumulated_scene_state: final held frame: exhaust trail, equation, summary line
